title: To Tackle Cost-Skew Tradeoff: An Adaptive Learning Approach for Hub Node Selection
problem: Clock tree skew is a critical performance limiter in chip design; achieving good balance between total wire-length cost and skew requires selecting optimal hub nodes, but this combinatorial optimization is hard to solve optimally at large scale.
motivation: Routing quality directly impacts clock distribution performance and power; effective hub node selection can improve the cost-skew tradeoff, particularly important for large-scale industrial designs.
method: The approach trains a reinforcement learning agent—a system that learns by trying different options and receiving feedback on results—to select hub nodes (central connection points) that balance two competing goals: keeping wiring cost low and keeping timing differences (clock skew) small. The agent explores different configurations, learning which selections better balance these tradeoffs. By adapting its strategy based on what works, it finds effective hub nodes without evaluating every possible combination.
key_novelty: Uses reinforcement learning—a system that learns by experimenting and adjusting its approach based on feedback—to automatically select hub nodes that balance wiring cost and clock timing differences.
contributions: Reinforcement learning formulation for hub node selection problem
Adaptive learning strategy enabling effective exploration-exploitation tradeoff
Demonstrated performance on both small and large-scale clock nets suitable for EDA integration
primary_theme: Adaptive RL-based clock tree hub node selection
